english.title: Possess goods with a false trade mark for sale / hire
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) with a view to gain for yourself or another, or with intent to cause loss to another, and without the consent of the proprietor, had in your possession, custody or control in the course of a business, goods, namely **(..SPECIFY GOODS..), which bore, or the packaging of which bore, a sign identical to, or likely to be mistaken for, a registered trade mark, namely **(..SPECIFY THE REGISTERED TRADE MARK..), with a view to you or another

(A)_[selling]_
(B)_[letting for hire]_
(C)_[offering or exposing for sale or hire]_
(D)_[distributing]_
(E)_[**(..WHERE MORE THAN ONE OF THE ABOVE OPTIONS IS REQUIRED PLEASE SPECIFY..)]_

the said goods
english.legislation: Contrary to section 92(1)(c) and (6) of the Trade Marks Act 1994.

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) IMPORTANT NOTE: In relation to any offence of making/selling counterfeit tapes/compact disc's/records of music, films or games, or the infringing of trade marks, the police service may obtain FREE expert advice and assistance in their investigations from the British Phonographic Industry Anti-Piracy Unit.
Furthermore the Anti Piracy Unit will arrange FREE OF CHARGE the forensic examination of computers etc, the preparation of the appropriate statements of evidence and the attendance of expert witnesses at court. For more information see the British Phonographic Industry.Officers of the Anti Piracy Unit may be contacted at ANY time.
In any enquiry relating to the manufacture or distribution of pirate films, including via the Internet, you can contact FACT (Federation Against Copyright Theft) who can provide you with assistance and advice. FACT has local investigators covering the whole of the UK and operates within the spirit of RIPA, Data Protection Act and Human Rights Act. FACT services include forensic examination of discs and computers, analysis of data using i2 software and NIM and the provision of training and intelligence on matters relating to film piracy.
(ii) See section 92(4) for exceptions and 92(5) for defence.
(iii) Section 103(2) provides that use of a sign identical to a trade mark is not limited to a graphic representation.
(iv) See section 101 if offence committed by a partnership or body corporate.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
